items.title: Game Awards 2026: All Game of the Year Front-Runners and Predictions
items.summary: What’s in pole position for gaming’s top prize? Let’s make some predictions
items.content:
By Oli Welsh Updated Oct 28, 2026, 11:40 PM EDT GOTY Watch What’s in pole position for gaming’s top prize? Let’s make some predictions

Image: S-Game Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover Sign in to your Polygon.com account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 52 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap We are getting to the business end of the competition for Game of the Year at the 13th Game Awards, set for Dec. 10; with only a couple of exceptions, most of the key competitors are out there. And it has to be said that the likelihood of anything emerging to stop Grand Theft Auto 6 from sweeping the night looks increasingly slim in what is turning out to be a much weaker year than it looked on paper.

At this point, we have a clear idea of what games will be favored by The Game Awards' voting body : A high Metacritic rating (preferably over 90) is a must; role-playing games and action-adventures are strongly favored, as are games with strong narrative elements; indie and multiplayer games struggle harder for recognition than AAA single-player adventures. We used these metrics to correctly predict last year's winner, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , and the 2024 winner, Astro Bot . In 2025, we also predicted all six GOTY nominees and correctly called 20 other categories.

Below, you'll find our predictions for the most likely nominees, of which there are six each year, for Game of the Year 2026 — taken only from games that have already been released (or made available for review). We'll update these rankings throughout the year as new games are released. We'll also list some likely upcoming contenders and some of the 2026 GOTY race's dark horses, too.

Update (Oct. 27): We've reached the end of October, but two key competitors are still yet to come: Grand Theft Auto 6 and Nintendo's remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time . Phantom Blade Zero has made a minor splash and shaken up the rankings; it seems like the final in the coffin of Crimson Desert 's hopes. And nominations for the Golden Joystick Awards' Ultimate Game of the Year award have been revealed — never a strong predictor for The Game Awards, but indicative of a few titles' momentum.

Resident Evil Requiem screenshot Image: Capcom Why it could win: Resident Evil is a reliable contender at The Game Awards , with three GOTY nominations since 2019, and many more in other categories. Requiem combines the fan appeal of the remakes with the freshness of a new entry, and blends their gameplay successfully, too. It's slickly produced, digestible, thrilling, with both global appeal and a serious side: a perfect Game Awards GOTY contender.

Weaknesses: Requiem 's critical reception was very good overall, but perhaps a tiny bit soft to be a true GOTY contender — it sits in the high 80s on Metacritic and OpenCritic. How well it fares in the long run will depend on the strength of the competition, but for now, it's in the lead.

Momentum (holding steady): Potential challengers to Requiem 's status as pack leader just keep falling by the wayside. Nothing else released this year combines critical acclaim with a perfect Game Awards genre profile so effectively, and nothing else will until GTA 6 comes out. It's a lock for a nomination.

Read Giovanni Colantonio's full review of Resident Evil Requiem .

Image: S-Game Why it could win: Phantom Blade Zero is this year's Black Myth: Wukong , a visually spectacular action game from an exciting new Chinese studio that muscled its way into the GOTY race. Unlike Black Myth , and unlike this year's Korean competitor Crimson Desert , it's got strong reviews (88 on Metacritic, 90 on OpenCritic).

Weaknesses: While it has reviewed well, Phantom Blade hasn't quite pulled away from a crowded action-adventure field that will be competing for the last couple of nominations, including Control Resonant and 007 First Light .

Momentum (new entry): Games like Phantom Blade Zero 's fortunes are powered by fan response; much depends on how it's received when it goes on general release.

Read Paulo Kawanishi's full review of Phantom Blade Zero .

Image: Intelligent Systems/Nintendo Why it could win: Reviews are very strong, at 89 on Metacritic. Critics love that Fortune's Weave has united strong storytelling with refined combat in a Fire Emblem game for the first time in a long time, and it helps that it's done so on an epic canvas. There's growing recognition at the TGAs for deep and authentic Japanese-developed RPGs like Metaphor: ReFantazio , and there's big fan support too: Fire Emblem: Three Houses was an unlikely winner of the Player's Voice award.

items.title: Final Fantasy Resonance and Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 success means "all signals" point to Square Enix making a mainline turn-based JRPG, analyst says: "Just a matter of time"
items.content:
"Square Enix has left a significant chunk of JRPG players behind" by focusing on action RPGs, he suggests

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Square Enix) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter As Final Fantasy Resonance has a strong start, and, like Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, proves what an appetite JRPG fans have for turn-based games, one analyst suggests that Square Enix "knows what it's missed out on" after its "move towards more action-oriented Final Fantasy titles."

Square Enix's new turn-based, HD-2D release launched last week and quickly dethroned Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth as the series' single-player games' highest concurrent player peak on Steam. And, as you might expect, that's translated to a lot of money for Square Enix, too.

According to Alinea Analytics analyst Rhys Elliott , Resonance has now sold 400k copies across PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S, bringing in $20 million in revenue. That's obviously rather a lot, and Elliott suggests it reflects what JRPG fans actually want and that Square Enix is catering to it. It's also worth keeping in mind that this doesn't include what the game made on the Nintendo Switch 2.

"Given the strong positive reaction to – and early sales of – Resonance and last year's Expedition 33 (which is tracking way better than recent Final Fantasy games), it's clear that Square Enix has left a significant chunk of JRPG players behind during their move towards more action-oriented Final Fantasy titles," he suggests.

"While Square chased more Western trends, a Western company swept in and released Expedition 33, a game JRPG fans wanted for decades and even won game of the year at The Game Awards," he continues. "Square knows this, knows what it's missed out on, and it's seen Capcom succeed on Steam with its legacy franchises where Square Enix has arguably floundered."

Final Fantasy Resonance is the second-biggest Steam launch of any turn-based RPG from Square Enix Final Fantasy Resonance is part of a "resurgence of turn-based RPGs and JRPGs," lead dev says Final Fantasy Resonance dethrones Rebirth for the series' largest Steam peak for a single-player RPG

Obviously, that isn't to say that Final Fantasy Resonance was made in response to Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, as it was in the works well before Sandfall's reveal, let alone its wildly successful launch last year. However, the timing of another turn-based RPG gaining so much traction can't be ignored, and Elliott suggests that Square Enix may consider altering its strategy going forward.

"I can see Square Enix going down a new route, with many diverging paths, for Final Fantasy," he explains. "They've already outlined their plans to go fully multiplatform, smartly moving away from timed PlayStation exclusivity.

"I can also see the company balancing its MMO, high-fidelity remakes, and big-budget mainline Final Fantasy titles with more of these smaller 2D-HD original pixel games alongside the 2D-HD remakes," he continues. "There's still a gap for a turn-based JRPG big-budget Final Fantasy, though, and all the signals are pointing Square Enix in that direction. Just a matter of time, I reckon."

It's not just Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 developer Sandfall that the analyst suggests Square Enix takes notes from, though. After a particularly stellar year with the likes of Resident Evil Requiem, Pragmata, and Onimusha: Way of the Sword – showcasing success with new IP and old favorites alike – Elliott adds: "I'd take even more cues from Capcom, if I were them."

Final Fantasy 14 devs say Evercold's new Evolved mode isn't massive power creep: "If you don't want to change, you don't have to."

Catherine Lewis Social Links Navigation Deputy News Editor I'm GamesRadar+'s Deputy News Editor, working alongside the rest of the news team to deliver cool gaming stories that we love. After spending more hours than I can count filling The University of Sheffield's student newspaper with Pokemon and indie game content, and picking up a degree in Journalism Studies, I started my career at GAMINGbible where I worked as a journalist for over a year and a half. I then became TechRadar Gaming's news writer, where I sourced stories and wrote about all sorts of intriguing topics. In my spare time, you're sure to find me on my Nintendo Switch or PS5 playing through story-driven RPGs like Xenoblade Chronicles and Persona 5 Royal, nuzlocking old Pokemon games, or going for a Victory Royale in Fortnite.

items.title: 6 Turn-Based RPGs That Are 10/10 Masterpieces
items.summary: RPGs like Clair Obscur prove that games with turn-based combat still have a place in the modern gaming ecosystem.
items.content:
Maelle looking up at the camera in Clair Obscur Expedition 33 Image via Sandfall Interactive Add CBR on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Sage Negron Published Oct 27, 2026, 8:45 PM EDT Sage Negron is a freelance writer based in New York City. He has contributed to CBR in the past, as well as Looper and DualShockers. When he's not writing, he's usually playing video games or reading a good book. Sign in to your CBR account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread 3 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Turn-based RPGs don't test reflexes and instead require players to rely on careful planning and strategy. While some titles in the genre have fairly simple combat systems, the best RPGs, like Clair Obscur , add new mechanics into the mix that make every battle feel engaging.

While action RPGs have become increasingly common, these RPGs prove there's still plenty of room for turn-based gameplay in today's ecosystem. From JRPGs to titles made in the West, these games prove exactly why turn-based RPGs are so compelling and are must-plays for anyone who enjoys the genre.

Magus Chrono Trigger Boss Battle Image Via Square Enix Few games have aged as well as Chrono Trigger , which is just as enjoyable now as it was when the game was first released back in 1995. While its turn-based combat system may seem fairly standard at first glance, the fact that enemies are visible on screen puts it ahead of games with random encounters from its era.

That said, the best thing about Chrono Trigger is its tech system, which allows two or three characters to team up and unleash powerful Double and Triple Tech attacks. This system naturally encourages players to experiment with different parties and use every character to their fullest.

The battle system in Metaphor: Refantazio is stylistic and dynamic like the Persona games but goes beyond them with its encouragement of making the first blow Image via Atlus Developer Atlus is well known for making exceptional turn-based RPGs, specifically those in the Shin Megami Tensei and Persona series. In 2024, they released an original game in that format titled Metaphor: Refantazio , and it proved that their formula works even outside jof their more popular franchises.

Players take control of a party of magical creatures fighting against a malevolent prince trying to usurp the throne of the fantasy land of Euchronia and spread darkness across the land. Like similar Atlus games, gameplay is divided between battling monsters in dungeons and spending time with party members to increase stats. Both are layered under a fantastic story filled with unexpected twists and over-the-top boss battles.

The game proudly embraces many of the fantasy genre tropes, while also offering a unique spin on the genre that only Atlus can pull off. Metaphor: Refantazio could be the start of a great franchise that continues on for years, or an amazing one-off experience that stands on its own. Either way, it’s still a fantastic game .

Sign in to claim your place on the leaderboard!

Image via Intelligent Systems The Fire Emblem franchise is one of the premier strategy RPGs currently on the market. Ever since Fire Emblem Awakening reinvigorated the franchise on the Nintendo 3DS, the series has enjoyed plenty of mainstream success. The first mainline entry for the Nintendo Switch, Fire Emblem: Three Houses , was another fine entry.

As a professor at a prestigious military school, there are three different students that players can take under their wing. This can lead to several different outcomes requiring multiple playthroughs to get the full experience. Each of these paths allows players to command different battalions in tactical turn-based combat.

All franchises have things that don't make sense, and the Fire Emblem has no shortage of head-scratching details.

items.title: 10 Best Turn-Based RPGs of All Time, Ranked
items.summary: Turn-based RPGs like Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 put action RPGs to shame.
items.content:
clair obscur expedition 33 featured art Image via Sandfall Interactive Add CBR on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Sage Ashford Published Oct 23, 2026, 5:45 PM EDT Staff Writer for CBR, Sage Ashford has also written for Comicon as well as other sites such as The Gamer, and has been doing freelance work since 2014, and been working for CBR since 2016. His focus is primarily on spreading the word on obscure anime, comic books, and games whenever possible. Follow him on Twitter @ sageshinigami, or on YouTube @ nolevelcap. Sign in to your CBR account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread 4 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Even though action RPGs are often seen as more modern than their turn-based counterparts, turn-based RPGs have made a comeback in recent years. Last year's Game of the Year, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, has turn-based combat, and the turn-based Persona games have begun to eclipse the now-action RPG Final Fantasy titles in popularity.

The greatest turn-based RPGs find ways to make their combat feel dynamic, creating addictive battle systems and wrapping them all in an amazing story. Some turn-based RPGs tell classic fantasy stories, while others feel more modern and even futuristic, but they're all great examples of how good the genre can be.

Ochette, Castti, Throne, Osvald, Partitio, Agnea, Hikari, and Temenos at a camp in a forest in Octopath Traveler II Image via Square-Enix Square-Enix tapped into the charm of the 16-bit era with their Octopath Traveler series. Yet there's more to the franchise than being a nostalgic throwback. Octopath Traveler II tells eight stories of eight travelers who just happen to find themselves working together as they overcome major obstacles in their lives.

While the first game is more of a testing ground, the second title improves on every aspect to create a generational classic. The game's combat is exceptional thanks to a mix of the franchise's Boost system and every enemy having specific weaknesses that players have to discover on their own. It naturally encourages players to build a balanced party and commit to big moves to finish enemies off.

Rip Mystery Packs of Graded Cards & Collectibles

Japanese Pokémon Center 20th Anniversary Promo · PSA 10

Must be 18+/19+ to participate depending on jurisdiction.

Image via Konami Suikoden V is one of the underrated classics of the PS2 era of gaming. Set in the Queendom of Falena, Suikoden V follows a prince trying to protect his family after his government is taken over in a coup. As ever with Suikoden games, the focus shifts away from the usual "save the world" plot and focuses on gathering a military capable of restoring peace to the land.

The Suikoden battle systems have always been fun thanks to the variety present. Suikoden V expands on the franchise's usual war battles, forcing players to learn how to wage war both on land and sea at the same time. Meanwhile, the duels remain just as intense as ever, while the six-on-six battles are unlike anything else on the market.

Sign in to claim your place on the leaderboard!

Super Mario RPG screenshot showing Mario, Mallow, Bowser, and Geon standing together while Mallow pointing at something Image via Nintendo Super Mario RPG: Legend of the Seven Stars is still just as fun today as it was when it was released. Despite a massive upgrade in graphics, it still retains the charm of the original and its cutesy, diorama settings for each stage. While the story isn't much to think about, the world-building given to the Mushroom Kingdom is awesome.

Though some people describe Super Mario RPG as an ideal RPG for newcomers , Square still managed to innovate with its combat. The timing-based attack and defense forced players to do more than just sit back and select options from a menu.

Players who mastered blocking at the right time could often avoid damage altogether, so there was plenty of incentive to get it right. The remake retains all of this and even adds some fun team attacks to shake things up.

Dragon Quest XI battle screenshot showing Erik blocking a high kick from Jade in the martial arts tournament Image via Square-Enix Dragon Quest XI is still the peak of traditional JRPG gaming, years later. It tells what feels like a traditional story early on, but adds enough twists and subversions for players to never really know where it's all going. Though it's one of the longer games out, it's also a delight to play, thanks to the variety in settings and the adorable Toriyama character designs.

items.title: Game Pass Is About To Lose Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 And Some Other Incredible Games
items.summary: The RPG sensation and more gems are leaving in October
items.content:
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was one of 2025’s best games and one of the best third-party releases ever to join Game Pass day-and-date. Players have now had over a year to finish the turn-based RPG, but for any subscribers who haven’t yet taken the plunge, time is running out. The GOTY winner is leaving Game Pass on October 15.

That leaves you just under two weeks to go and complete the journey or start it from scratch. You can rush the main story to clear it in under 30 hours, but if you want to mine all of the expanded content, a completionist run will take you more than twice that. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is one of the rare JRPG-inspired games that’s managed to break through in the modern era to a broader audience, in part thanks to its novel dodge and parry mechanics which inject some fresh energy into the usual turn-based grind. It’s also worth making it all the way through to hit the twist ending .

But Clair Obscur is also not the only great game leaving Game Pass this month . The full list includes:

Pacific Drive and A Plague Tale Requiem are both excellent, especially for the spooky month. The former is a sci-fi survival crafting game about navigating a zone full of strange anomalies with a haunted station wagon. The latter is about surviving a late medieval Europe infested with disease carrying rats. Donut County , on the other hand, is a light hearted puzzle game you can finish in just a few hours that is still one of my favorite indie games of all time.

items.title: Eight Games Are Leaving Xbox Game Pass In Early October 2026
items.content:
Microsoft has revealed the next eight games leaving Xbox Game Pass in early October 2026, with all of these being highlighted as "leaving soon" on the official Xbox phone app.

It's a particularly painful one this month. Our early predictions were pretty accurate, if you ask me. We got four games spot on with Donut County , Evil West , The Casting of Frank Stone , and Pacific Drive all on the chopping block this October, but including Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is tres merde.

Here's the full list of games set to leave Xbox Game Pass in early October 2026:

You'll find discounts of at least 20% on all of these Xbox Game Pass titles until they leave on October 15th.

If you've not tried it yet, I'd absolutely recommend giving Expedition 33 a go. It's an all-timer, no question about it. Also, with the inclusion of the Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy in recent months, I think if you want the full picture, perhaps consider giving Requiem a go before it gommages too.

We're just days into October at this point and there's lots more to come. The likes of Gears of War: E-Day are on the way, as well as the highly-anticipated Valor Mortis . So, be sure to check out our Xbox Game Pass guide for the month !

items.content:
Expeditioners!

Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text!

This brings the total number of supported languages to 20!

With the new Arabic language support, we had to consider additional changes to the game’s UI to ensure a smooth and enjoyable experience for Arabic-speaking players around the world.

Adding Arabic localization has been a true team effort over many months, from the incredible adaptation and localization work carried out by the linguists, to reworking the vast majority of the user interface for right-to-left reading, all the way through localization testing.

Every team involved brought passion and dedication to making this possible, and we couldn’t be more grateful for their work. We hope this update makes the story feel even more personal to our players.

Today’s update also includes some additional fixes and improvements. Read the full patch notes here!

Thank you all so much for your continued support! <3

Tomorrow comes.

~ The Expedition 33 Team

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Devs Won't Pick a Canon Ending as They Work on a Sequel: 'It Is a Schrodinger's Ending'
items.summary: This is an article about one of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's writers saying that the developers will not "canonize" one ending over the other, even as they work on future games set in the same universe.
items.content:
If you've finished Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , you probably have some strong opinions about the game's multiple possible endings. I feel like saying anything more about that at the top of this article would be irresponsible, but this is a story about one of the game's writers saying that developer Sandfall Interactive is not going to "canonize" one ending over the other, even as they work on future games set in the same universe.

As such, from now on, I'm going to talk as if you have beaten the game and seen at least one of the two endings. Huge spoilers for the ending of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 below the video! Read on at your own risk.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 offers two possible endings no matter how you choose to play the game or how much side content you do. At the end of the game, you can choose to control Maelle or Verso in a single battle against the other, and winning it gets you the ending of whichever character you picked. Already tragic enough, neither of these endings are very satisfying ones. Verso's ending offers emotional catharsis for both characters admittedly, but at the expense of the lives of most of the rest of the cast you've come to love up to that point. Maelle's keeps everyone alive and kicking, but at the cost of multiple people's free will and, arguably, Maelle's own life and sanity. The choice is rough, but also very much in keeping with who Verso and Maelle have shown themselves to be in the game up to this point.

But that does beg the question: which of these endings in the "real" or canon ending? You could argue that it doesn't matter, and it's up to the player, but developer Sandfall Interactive has confirmed it's working on another game in the same universe. It seems likely that at some point the story of any future game they make could brush up against the consequences of one choice or the other. And if that happens, they'll have to pick which option is the truly "canon" version. Right? Right?

Wrong, says writer Jennifer Svedberg-Yen in an interview I conducted at DICE Summit last month. "We are not going to pick one," she told me. When I pushed, asking if they'd truly never choose, she replied: "Never say never, but there is no canon ending there. It is a Schrodinger's ending."

Expedition 33's two tragic endings were apparently settled on by the writers early in the development process, according to Svedberg-Yen. They knew they wanted Maelle and Verso to fight, she says, and neither of them really care much for "storybook" happy endings.

"I think that was almost like an unspoken agreement," she continued. "We never even considered really a true, happy ending. I think there was maybe a happier one possibly. You can see also in the way that the endings are edited, that one has a slightly more uplifting tone and one has a slightly darker tone. That was a choice that Guillaume made in terms of just having a little bit of shading there. But from my perspective, narratively, both are equally valid. Both are both good and bad. And it really just depends on whose perspective, whose good or whose happily-ever-after you are prioritizing."

I guess at least that means Verso's ending gets to continue being canon in my own, personal mental lore.

We spoke to Svedberg-Yen on a number of other subjects, including the wild, winding road she took to becoming a writer on Expedition 33, the emotional inspiration for each of the main characters, and the silly bets her colleagues lost because the game did so well . You can read our full interview with her right here.

Rebekah Valentine is a senior reporter for IGN. Got a story tip? Send it to rvalentine@ign.com.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is '95 percent' made with Blueprints
items.summary: Sticking to a nearly-vanilla version of Unreal Engine kept Sandfall Interactive on track.
items.content:
Keep up with the latest news, interviews, talk coverage, and other game dev insights from GDC right here on Game Developer. Read More

Sticking to a nearly-vanilla version of Unreal Engine kept Sandfall Interactive on track.

Much has been made of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 developer Sandfall Interactive's production process. As you've probably heard by now, the smash hit game was produced by a studio that employs fewer than 40 people, and everyone in the game industry has a hot take about what made that possible (and often ignore the hundreds of other people listed in the game's credits ).

They've been so prolific that at a GDC Festival of Gaming talk from Sandfall chief technical officer Tom Guillermin and senior gameplay programmer Florian Torres had an entire slide advising the audience not to use their presentation as a roadmap. "This is not meant to be a tutorial or like a how-to guide on how to make games," said Guillermin. "It's a retrospective on how we made Expedition 33 ."

But let's face it, when your studio's first game is such a highly-polished hit, everyone will obviously be trying to copy your homework. Developers aiming to learn about Sandfal's process swarmed Moscone West, and let out a collective murmur of shock when Guillermin and Torres described how their small team of programmers supported such an expensive-looking game—they just used a near-vanilla version of Unreal Engine.

Related: Clair Obscur writer shares production advice that could improve your game's story

And they didn't use Unreal Engine to write lines and lines and lines of code in C++. Expedition 33 was largely made with Unreal's Blueprints system.

According to Torres, 95 percent of the game was constructed in Blueprints.

For the uninitiated, Unreal Engine's Blueprints system is a visual scripting tool that lets developers link "nodes" together to create different gameplay elements. It's used to define object-oriented objects or classes in the game engine. For laypeople, this mean it lets developers assemble game logic by stringing together nodes of scripting logic without constantly coding in C++.

On Clair Obscur , this meant that Guillermin, Torres, and the rest of the programmers could hand off content and feature development to the studio's designers and artists, allowing them to produce and test content in the game engine with fewer roadblocks that would rely on a programmer to create code.

Unreal Engine developers use Blueprints to different degrees. The system is deeply tied into Unreal Engine's natural codebase, and if you need to modify the engine in any way, the system becomes less reliable. In fact Guillermin said that Sandfall has a very "vanilla-first" approach when it comes to using Unreal. "We take all the tools that are natively present and we push them to their to their limits so we don't have to develop bespoke tools for the features and content of the of the game," he said.

Related: Anthropic orders AI tool Claude to stop remaking video games

Photo via the author, slide by Sandfall Interactive

The only "modifications" they used were old-fashioned Unreal plugins like CommonUI, GeometryScripting, ALS (Advanced Locomotion System) and KawaiiPhysics (which one commentator on Bluesky described as "one guy's freeware project for doing swooshy anime hair physics.")

items.summary: Introducing a special bundle featuring the award‑winning fantasy RPG “Metaphor: ReFantazio”, created by the team behind Persona 3-5, paired with “Clair Obscur: Expedition 33” - now available at 10% off! Enjoy both titles and experience the
items.content:
Introducing a special bundle featuring the award‑winning fantasy RPG “Metaphor: ReFantazio”, created by the team behind Persona 3-5, paired with “Clair Obscur: Expedition 33” - now available at 10% off!

Enjoy both titles and experience the worlds for yourself!

The Metaphor: ReFantazio × Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Bundle includes two games: “Metaphor: ReFantazio” and “Clair Obscur: Expedition 33.”

Message from Guillaume Broche & Katsura Hashino

"Metaphor: ReFantazio is a game that is really inspiring for us. It tells a beautiful story in a completely new world that is masterfully crafted. It deals with heavy themes but one that resonates strongly with me is the importance of imagination in all aspects of our lives. The cast is lovable and the turn-based battle system is one of the best I have played. The re-imagination of the traditional jobs system through Archetypes is fantastic and opens up so many playstyles that are fun to play around with. On top of that, the game has one of the most charismatic villains I've ever seen in an RPG. It is a great honor to be able to collaborate with Atlus on this bundle, as I have been a fan of their work since Shin Megami Tensei: Lucifer's Call (also known as Shin Megami Tensei III Nocturne for some players)." - Guillaume Broche

"I am Katsura Hashino from ATLUS, serving as the Creative Director for “Metaphor: ReFantazio.” I am very pleased to hear that a Steam bundle will be released with “Expedition 33,” a title that has received high praise around the world.

“Expedition 33” is a work that conveys a deep understanding of and sincere dedication to the JRPG genre, crafted with great care down to the finest details. As someone who also creates RPGs, I found it to be truly inspiring.

I am genuinely delighted to see Japanese-style RPGs being born and embraced, not only from Japanese-based studios like ours, but other places around the world through diverse creative approaches.

While the two titles differ in their worlds and overall direction, players may find a shared spirit in how we each approach and express the RPG genre. I hope that this bundle encourages players to experience both titles and enjoy the breadth of what RPGs can offer."

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 | Dev Blog - Photo Mode
items.summary: Expeditioners, We're so pleased to see so many of you enjoying the new photo mode feature!! We put a lot of time and care into building this feature and we’re so glad to see so many of you enjoying it! There were a lot of moving parts invol
items.content:
Expeditioners,

We're so pleased to see so many of you enjoying the new photo mode feature!!

We put a lot of time and care into building this feature and we’re so glad to see so many of you enjoying it! There were a lot of moving parts involved in getting the Photo Mode set up, so we thought we’d show a bit of the process in this blog and talk a bit about what went into building this feature.

There were a few key people involved in the development of this, and each of them had a part to write here !

VINCENT CONSTANTIN-TURKI – Producer \

One of the main features we wanted to introduce with the Thank You Update was Photo Mode. It felt like a meaningful way to give something back to the players and thank them for their commitment to the game.

What’s funny is that the team in charge of developing Photo Mode doesn’t usually use this feature in other games, which is why we decided to collaborate with Shinobi. He helped us design a Photo Mode that would truly resonate with players.

NAJA DALMAGNE – QA Coordinator \

In many games we tested, Photo Modes often felt restrictive, which could quickly become frustrating. So, from the very beginning, one of the key goals we all agreed on was to give players as much freedom as possible. It was really about letting players express their creativity without getting in the way.

During development, the QA team ran into some unexpected and sometimes quite funny issues. One of the funniest, but also one of the most severe, involved characters whose heads or torsos could become displaced or deformed when opening the Photo Mode if they hadn’t been visible on screen for a while during exploration.

One feature I’m particularly proud of is the lighting system Florian worked on. It offers great flexibility while remaining fairly easy to use, which really makes a difference when you're trying to get the perfect shot.

FLORIAN TORRES – Senior Gameplay Programmer \ \

I love giving players as many tools and features as possible (that’s literally the purpose of my job).

When we started working on the photo mode, our goal was to give players as few restrictions as possible and that’s what I was in charge of coding: infinite camera distance, the ability to pass through collisions, lots of customizable lights, many (weird) filters, and more.

Of course, that comes with its challenges, but in the end it allows players to see a lot of things we don’t want to show during normal gameplay. The photo mode became a way to peek behind the scenes of each cinematic or environment, and sometimes even see how we have created the entire game.

Ever wondered what happens outside the camera frame? Here’s an example (sorry cinematic team, I love you).

LUDOVIC ‘SHINOBI’ HELME – Photo Mode Consultant \

We felt it was important to include anything that increases the “freedom” factor for players. It opens up countless possibilities every time someone enters photo mode: a very generous camera range to capture unseen details or create epic compositions, RGB curves control to edit and build your own color schemes, a strong custom lighting system to truly take ownership of a scene, and solid depth-of-field management.

But when all of that is also available in cutscenes - giving access to those incredible facial expressions and emotions - that’s when I really start to feel satisfied.

Every shot I’ve seen has blown my mind, and I often wish I’d been the one to come up with the idea. It’s truly inspiring.

I’m very proud that the team managed to create a tool that is both beginner-friendly and deeply satisfying for more experienced photographers. Finding that balance is extremely difficult.

With all of these features, there had to be a user-friendly way for people to make use of everything. Making sure players had full control of all the settings and could navigate all the features comes down to our awesome Gameplay & UI Programmer, VICTOR BOULEZ.

Thank you for all of your appreciation and feedback on this feature, we had a lot of fun making it and even more fun watching you use it!

This past week, especially, we’ve really loved the work you’ve all been putting into the social Photo Mode Prompt Challenge!! We’ve seen some amazing photography this past week, it’s completely blown our minds how creative you have been able to get with the prompts and tools.

Even though the challenge is over, feel free to keep sharing your work with us on social media, we thoroughly enjoy seeing some of your masterpieces!!

In the meantime, we are continuing to work on fixes for ongoing problems, keep an eye on the bug thread and socials to stay updated on the latest.

Finally, we leave you with some of our favourite uses of photo mode.

items.title: Hotfix 1.5.1 is live!
items.summary: Bug Fixes & Improvements Expeditioners, the 1.5.1 hotfix is now live! Thanks to your reports, we have worked on a number of fixes listed below: Gameplay Fixed Monoco’s weapon “Cannaro” being unobtainable from Chromatic Machinapieds Players
items.content:
Bug Fixes & Improvements

Expeditioners, the 1.5.1 hotfix is now live!

Thanks to your reports, we have worked on a number of fixes listed below:

Gameplay

  • Fixed Monoco’s weapon “Cannaro” being unobtainable from Chromatic Machinapieds

    • Players who already defeated the boss will automatically receive the weapon in their inventory, unless they started a NG+(+) after that

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Fixed Esquim not applying Mark to all enemies when a skill had 0 hits.

    [/*]

  • Fixed a targeting issue caused by using a Recoat item followed by ‘Retry Battle’, which resulted in the player being unable to target the middle enemy or character.

    [/*]

  • Fixed a soft-lock when attempting to load a save without hovering any slot while backup saves were displayed.

    [/*]

  • Fixed upgrade of the weapons to level 34 when spamming Upgrade weapon and change character buttons

    • Level 34 weapons have been reverted back to level 33

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Fixed character being able to use other characters' weapon when quickly switching weapon tabs after changing weapon

    [/*]

Environment

  • Nerfed the hardest boss in Verso’s Drafts (red lifebuoy) by moving it slightly to make a quest easier.

    [/*]

  • Fixed various environment issues (collisions, misplaced assets, missing or incorrect footsteps SFX) across Verso's Drafts, the World Map, and other levels.

    [/*]

Audio & Music

  • Improved environmental ambiances and spatial audio for better immersion in Verso’s Drafts

    [/*]

  • Enhanced audio mixes for select characters, combos, and finishers

    [/*]

  • Multiple audio & music issues were resolved, including:

    • Missing music after defeating new Endless Tower bosses.

      [/*]

    • Missing subtitle line for Sciel in one of the new cinematics.

      [/*]

    • Missing Barbapapa status effect SFX when receiving a second stack.

      [/*]

    • Missing some SFX for Licorne enemy in Verso’s Drafts.

      [/*]

    • Missing SFX for Paint Cage explosions in Verso's Drafts.

      [/*]

    • Music and SFX not pausing when opening pause menu during cinematic sequence with slow motion enabled, resulting in audio desynchronization for the remainder of the cinematic sequence

      [/*]
    [/*]

Localization

Fixed various localization issues, including:

  • Subtitles in Root Of All Evil cinematics disappearing too fast.

    [/*]

  • Overlapping text in Pictos & Luminas lists.

    [/*]

  • Autoplay dialogue options swapped when the title is set to LATAM Spanish.

    [/*]

  • Incorrect text displayed during Flying Manor side quest when the title is set to Vietnamese.

    [/*]

  • Verso’s skill Phantom Stars displaying HTML in combat when the title is set to Vietnamese.

    [/*]

Other

We are aware of various issues encountered, particularly the one reported by some of you who are having difficulty launching the title on Windows 11.

One of these issues is caused by Windows Security reporting false positives when launching. This has been fixed as part of the v1.5.1 hotfix as of 17:00 CET.

The other issue causing this problem is related to the Windows Smart App Control feature. Turning it off to fix it is not recommended as this will remove the feature permanently from your system. We are investigating this issue and hope to resolve it as soon as possible so we suggest waiting for the next hotfix!

Until then, 

Tomorrow comes!

And as always thanks for your support and for your reports via the official Typeform!

~ The Expedition 33 Team 

Update 08/01

We've pushed a fix for the soft lock occurring when Braseleur hits the player with orbs during two consecutive enemy turns.
